ground_truth.unit: log points of annualised household electricity consumption (kWh)
ground_truth.context: Table 2 ("Effect of the Reform on Residential Electricity Consumption and Expenditure (2011-2014)"), column (1), row Reform (T): the paper's difference-in-differences estimate of the August 2013 Spanish electricity pricing reform (fixed charge raised, regulated volumetric rate cut) on household electricity consumption, estimated by OLS.  Data: Spanish Household Budget Survey households interviewed between August 2011 and April 2014, each interviewed twice, in the same two-week period of two consecutive years; the control group has both interviews before the reform, the treated group its second interview after it.  T is the post-reform dummy for interviews whose electricity bill falls under the reform (the paper places the response one month after the reform, when households receive a reformed bill).  Dependent variable: log of electricity consumption in the month before the interview (kWh, annualised by the survey).  Regressors: T, log household price per kWh (expenditure divided by consumption), log income and its square, months since reform, and controls for household size, number of rooms, dwelling surface, elderly members, education of the household head, household economic situation (number of economically active members), renting, building older than 25 years, municipality-size dummies, urban area, province capital, regional dummies, quarterly dummies and year fixed effects.  No household fixed effects.  Standard errors clustered at the household level.

i4r.notes: Team 49 blanket verdict (code reproduces the paper's output); no meta-database row for column 1.

recomputed.notes: Outside tolerance: reproduced=-0.11934 vs claimed=-0.178 (relative error 32.96%, tolerance 15.17%, the ±1·SE band with SE=0.027).

cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: Treatment T is the dataset's T2 (=TT199): 1 for post-reform interviews from September 2013 on (months-since-reform dist 1-7). This matches Table 1 (T mean 0.19 overall, 0.50 in the treated group) and eq. (3); the alternative TT202, which codes the September 2013 (first reformed bill) interviews as 0, was not used.

Price, income and instruments are the prepared real (deflated by the time price index IP) variables in the analysis file: lnPRE (= ln p_kWh - IP), lny and lny2 (= ln y - IP and its square), and the instruments lnPRE_papas_, lnPRE_aguav_, lnPRE_gascar_ (effective prices of potatoes, water, fuel, with missing values already filled by the file's cell averages, so the IV sample equals the OLS sample).

LIML is coded by hand as a k-class estimator (fixest has no LIML); household FE versions use the within (demeaned) transformation, which gives LSDV point estimates. LIML SEs are a hand-coded household-clustered sandwich; they are not scored.

Controls: household size (NMIEMB), rooms (NHABIT), surface (SUPERF), elderly dummy (mayores), education of head (ESTUDREDSP, 4 levels), economic situation (SITUACTHOG_j, 3 levels), renting (alqui), building >25 years (edif25), municipality size (TAMAMU, 5 levels), urban, province capital (CAPROV), region (CCAA), quarter (trim), months since reform (dist), year FE; no survey weights. Retirement-income dummy not included (not in the paper's control list for eq. 4).

Sample: the 25,775 panel observations with non-missing T2, restricted to complete cases on all regression variables (mainly SITUACTHOG_j and SUPERF missing); n_obs and n_households are counted on that complete-case sample, singleton households included.
cell.notes: Two exploratory runs (variable listing; panel structure and variable definitions, no RESULT lines), then one estimation run, which is the final scored run. No error repairs, no claim comparisons. Paper read for method only. Readme.pdf in the mount was not opened. The FE-IV first stage is weak (cluster-robust Wald F about 10.6), so the IV columns are imprecise.
